media.title: Staszic School, Warsaw — architectural view, 1916
media.description: Printed architectural view of the purpose-built Staszic School at historical Polna 60 (now Noakowskiego 6), published in April 1916 while the building was still being completed. The original caption identifies the design as the work of architects Marian Kontkiewicz and Stanisław Zaleski.
media.altText: Printed grayscale architectural view of the four-storey Staszic School façade in Warsaw, with a Renaissance-inspired attic and small figures near the entrances.
media.publicCaption: Architectural view of the Staszic School at historical Polna 60, now Noakowskiego 6, Warsaw, published in 1916 after plans by Marian Kontkiewicz and Stanisław Zaleski.

places.displayName: Stanisław Staszic Gymnasium, Polna 60 / Noakowskiego 6, Warsaw
places.authorizedName: Gimnazjum im. Stanisława Staszica w Warszawie, ul. Polna 60
places.publicNote: School associated with Kaper’s secondary education and matura, identified as Gimnazjum im. Stanisława Staszica w Warszawie. The building carries two addresses for the same site: ul. Polna 60 in Kaper’s school years, and ul. Noakowskiego 6 after part of Polna Street was renamed for Stanisław Noakowski in 1938. Warszawa1939.pl documents it under the later address, and its bibliography pairs both forms. Built in 1914–16, burned after the Warsaw Uprising and rebuilt with an added storey, so the standing structure is not the pre-war fabric. The coordinates indicate the address area.
